newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: High NZD cuts seafood export earnings by NZ$60 mln.
newsitem.headline: High NZD cuts seafood export earnings by NZ$60 mln.

text.p: "Overvaluation" of the New Zealand dollar cut export earnings from seafood by NZ$60 million or nearly five percent in 1996, the New Zealand Fishing Industry Board said on Thursday.

Exports fell to $1.18 billion, down 4.74 percent from $1.24 billion in 1995. The volume of seafood exports rose 1.4 percent, meaning that the simple average return per tonne fell by 6.1 percent, the board said.
"The export results bear out the pain being felt by the fishing industry from the overvalued New Zealand dollar," board deputy chief executive Alastair Macfarlane said.

"Only four years ago the industry was confidently expecting to reach $2 billion in annual export returns by the turn of the century. Last year the board revised the target down to $1.65 billion, provided that a six percent annual growth rate could be maintained. The result for 1996 suggests that even that target is overly optimistic," he said.
